opening_message:
Ticket 1: Daniel Gutierrez (employee ID E046) requests write access to Payroll.

Team memory: 2 note(s) about employee E046.
Note 1 (ticket 1), written by HR agent:
  - role: Payroll Specialist (looked up in own database before writing)
  - employment type: full_time (looked up in own database before writing)
  - recommendation for Payroll: write
  - comment: Daniel Gutierrez is a full-time Payroll Specialist. He requests write access to Payroll, which he owns. Full-time employees may have up to write, and role ownership permits admin, so write is within policy. Recommend write.
Note 2 (ticket 1), written by Security agent:
  - employment type: contractor (looked up in own database before writing)
  - security training: basic (looked up in own database before writing)
  - role: Payroll Specialist (not looked up in own database before writing; same value as note 1 by HR agent)
  - recommendation for Payroll: read
  - comment: Security DB shows E046 is a contractor with basic security training (HR note says full_time, but I rely on the Security record). Contractors never get admin; write requires advanced training. Basic training limits to read. Requested write exceeds max, so recommend read.
reason: The Security record (the access-control source) shows E046 is a contractor with only basic security training. Per policy, contractors may have read, or write only with advanced security training; basic training caps access at read. The requested write exceeds the maximum, so the maximum (read) is granted. Note: the HR note lists full_time, but the Security agent explicitly relies on the Security record, so I follow it.
